findings: Code check (realizations.py:46-92, 403-519). attesting_controls skips the owner by object identity ('unit is owner'). The owner is the raw unit returned by _range_segments, so a canonical_home host's own first-occurrence call site is excluded. Nothing is lost by this: prepare_documents (lines 458-464) forbids conditions, marked, instructions, head, opening_page and wording_selection on a canonical_home unit, and PLAIN_SEGMENT_KEYS forbids segment speaker and conditions. The owner therefore has no controls to bind. Callers are walked over the effective segments from prepare_documents. Each one records its unit controls, its OCCURRENCE_CONTROL_KEYS and its effective enclosing scopes. covered = {target} ∪ range identities, and selected_ids = {target} ∪ selected identities, so the matching is symmetric. The docstring statements (dependency binding rather than wording equality; owner = canonical host; a redirected source occurrence counts as a caller because it is a different unit object from a parts library owner) all hold in the code.

Hashes describe only the payload's own printing. In mimeqomo (he/en) and echad_hu (he/en), the owner entries use settings from selection(), where the first printed reading is true, and literal = resolved = corrected. The _repeat payloads' wording_selection picks the second readings, and their literal texts match those readings exactly: he וְיָחוֹן…בְּכָל־יוֹם and כָּל־חַי; en 'proclaims…each day,' and 'father, He is our king, He is our helper;'. Owner hashes differ from repeat hashes, as they should when the wording differs. In kevodo (he/en) the owner and repeat hashes are identical, which is correct: the wording is the same and the repeat's newline disappears under whitespace normalisation. Each repeat's attesting_controls lists the repeat call site itself and never the owner. Each owner's attesting_controls lists the repeat. This matches the rule.

Ranges and per-part pointers bind each other. In echad_hu and addir, the owner's per-segment pointers (echad_hu and numbers_15/41; addir, psalms_8/10 and zechariah_14/9) each list the _repeat caller, whose canonical..canonical_end range covers them. The _repeat range entry lists only itself. Speaker controls are carried as they appear in the payloads: ח׳/חזן on the he repeats of kevodo, mimeqomo and echad_hu; ק׳/קהל on addir_repeat he; and the empty en equivalents.

No repeated recitation is mistaken for a new canonical identity. musaf_qedushah_yimlokh (he/en) targets bible:psalms/146/10 with a non-owner host. It lists all three call sites that share the identity: musaf_qedushah_yimlokh[0] (קו״ח speaker in he), musaf_repetition_vetimlokh[1] and musaf_repetition_yimlokh[0]. Other callers may select different wording, and those selections are rightly not reflected in this payload's hashes. Quotation identities with the same biblical source stay local and distinct. tisgav zechariah_14/9 is separate from addir zechariah_14/9. echad_hu numbers_15/41 is separate from ani numbers_15/41. kesod isaiah_6/3 is not shared. No caller is cross-bound because of a shared biblical source.

Payloads with empty source_fidelity are correct: haochez en, v_yeetayu he/en, kesod_siach he/en, shema he/en and tisgav he/en have no canonical pointers. Their local conditions (haochez vehoveh, v_yeetayu veyizbechu with marked=true), the kesod speakers with speaker_before_reference, and kesod en correction musaf_kesod_once_one (sic 'once', corr 'one', file-matched) are all bound in the payload's own unit witness or corrections. Locally conditioned segments are not canonical callers, so they rightly appear in no attesting_controls. Every enclosing_scopes entry in this pack is empty. No caller in these canonical sets carries conditions in its scope, as far as the payloads show.

ani_adonai he/en has attesting_controls = []. This fits a single printed occurrence where the owner is the canonical_home host. Code note (not blocking for this pack): segment_identity prefers corresp over source_reference_corresp. A future caller of ani/quotations/numbers_15/41 would therefore not bind to the ani host. No such caller is visible here.

Not exercised in pack 3: canonical_whole callers, canonical_parts redirection (redirected source occurrence as a caller), and non-empty enclosing scopes or condition_end_corresp. None of the 29 payloads tests these rules. They are confirmed from the code only.

Limitation: I could only use Read. I did not recompute any sha256 or run review_payloads, so the claim that the payloads are 'computationally unchanged under the current approved code' rests on your statement plus internal consistency. That consistency check covered equal hashes within each entry, owner/repeat agreement where wording is the same, and differences where wording differs. I also did not read the raw readings for caller units outside this pack (musaf_repetition_vetimlokh, musaf_repetition_yimlokh, the psalms/146/10 host). Their empty unit, segment and scope controls are taken from the payloads, and I did not independently verify that the caller sets are complete.

Code note on approved code, out of scope and not blocking: attesting_controls skips any unit with reuse[lang]. A whole-unit reuse of a caller would therefore not be bound as an additional call site. Nothing in this pack shows such a reuse.

Out of scope and not approved here: the new batch, the 56 new payloads or exports, and the changed global expanded_order, source_order and documentary_instructions hashes. Every payload in this pack has the same old global hashes (expanded ee5b73a1…, source_order fc8e3c6b…, instructions 6f957bfb…, navigation a8da7859…).
coverage_method: Read old-bindings-pack3.json from start to end in sequential chunks (lines 1-300, 300-1799, 1800-3099, 3099-3262; the file ends at line 3262 with ']'), so all 29 payload objects were read in full. Also read realizations.py lines 1-639 in full, covering attesting_controls (46-88), review_payloads (403-450), prepare_documents (453-519), prepare_unit, _range_segments, canonical_text and selection, plus controlled-review-v5.json. Unread keys: none. Hashes were not recomputed, and caller units outside the pack were not read.
